notes: Persistent data protection keychain items in a signed .app carrying an embedded Development provisioning profile. A bare signed CLI is killed at exec by AMFI (rc=137), because kSecAttrAccessControl routes through the data protection keychain, which needs the restricted keychain-access-groups entitlement that only a provisioning profile authorizes. So the real macOS app must be a provisioned app, not a helper CLI or daemon. Team 7W8527FJJE, access group 7W8527FJJE.com.connetto.probe. N1 was also confirmed independently via an ephemeral Secure Enclave key from a plain signed CLI (no provisioning needed for that path).

notes: N1 against N3 is the upstream question. RequireUserPresence maps to the userPresence access-control flag and here matches N1 on all three points (prompt, passcode fallback, survival of a fingerprint change), so on macOS apple-native-keyring-store suffices and nothing needs contributing upstream. Same provisioned .app requirement as N1 and N2, since this library forces the data protection keychain.

provider: iCloud Keychain and Google Password Manager

Q12.value: failure mode observed. After quitting and reopening the browser, an assertion scoped to the stored non-discoverable credential id was offered only over the cross-device path (a phone QR), with no on-device Touch ID option. Forcing the internal transport then returned NotAllowedError and Safari reported no local passkey for the origin, so there was no on-device copy to use. A user without a second device could not authenticate. Confounders: dozens of passkeys for one origin and user, mid-test fingerprint-set changes, and a cache clear. The earlier fresh single-session runs did assert locally with stable bytes, so persistence of the secret holds, but reliable on-device re-assertion after a restart did not.

Q13.value: demonstrated more strongly than the formal clear-site-data test. The identical PRF output 712f0c24...e05ea5 appeared in both Firefox and Safari on the same Mac, two different browser profiles, so the credential and its PRF secret live in iCloud Keychain outside any single browser profile. Clearing one browser's site data cannot remove a credential another browser already reads

Q11a.value: WebAuthn creation is impossible inside a dedicated worker, PublicKeyCredential is undefined there. Confirmed on every browser row

Q11b.value: topology viable. The HKDF key imported from the PRF bytes survived a structured-clone transfer into a worker (key survived transfer=true), the worker derived with it (worker derived=true), and raw export failed in both the page and the worker (non-extractable). Derived bits 6a9b02ed48a9e2b344afd51a7d55fd2bdd1a49e12bf66863555f00f6b8600640

notes: Durability. Q13 (credential lives outside the browser profile) is proven by cross-browser byte identity, the strongest form. Q12 surfaced a real failure mode rather than a clean pass: after a browser restart the platform passkey was offered only cross-device (QR), and forcing on-device transport gave NotAllowedError with no local passkey shown, so a user without a second device could be locked out. This is the risk the operator flagged. It is confounded by heavy test churn (many same-user passkeys, fingerprint changes, cache clear) and does not reproduce the earlier clean single-session Touch ID asserts, so it is a risk to design against, not a proven everyday breakage. The PRF secret itself is persistent (synced passkey), the issue is the browser's willingness to offer the local credential after a restart. Q11 topology fully answered: creation cannot happen in a worker (Q11a), but a derived CryptoKey survives transfer to a worker, is usable there, and is non-exportable (Q11b), so the browser design has a viable worker topology.
